tips.title: Panel Line Scribing with RB Productions
tips.text: For deep, consistent panel lines, use RB Productions' scribing tools. Start with a medium grit sanding stick to lightly score the panel lines on your ICM or Arma Hobby kit. Then, using the RB Productions scriber, press gently and pull towards you in one smooth motion. Use the curved and straight scribers for different panel types. Wipe away any debris with a soft brush after each pass.

tips.title: Bending Photo-Etch with Eduard Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch bending jigs make complex shapes achievable. Soak the photo-etch part in warm water for 15-20 seconds, then carefully slide it into the jig, bending it gradually. Use gentle pressure and don't overbend — you can always add more bend later if needed. Once the desired shape is achieved, let it dry in the jig for at least 2 hours before removing.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Guard
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush needle and nozzle in top condition with the Iwata Brush Guard cleaning kit. After each painting session, disassemble the nozzle-fan and needle. Using the Iwata Brush Guard's wire brush, scrub the needle gently to remove any dried paint. Follow up with the included pipe cleaner for a thorough clean. Reassemble and test-spray before your next session.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: For sharp, clean edges, use Tamiya tape for masking large areas and Kabuki tape for fine details. Tamiya tape adheres well to flat surfaces, while Kabuki tape's thinner width and better adhesion make it ideal for complex shapes. Cut Kabuki tape with a sharp hobby knife and GodHand nippers for precise trimming. Press down edges firmly to prevent paint bleeding.

tips.title: Sanding Sticks Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Achieve a smooth surface on your styrene models with a progression of sanding sticks. Start with a coarse grit to remove major imperfections, followed by medium and fine grits. Wet-sand using a damp cloth or sponge, applying gentle pressure in circular motions. Wipe away debris after each grit, and use a tack cloth or compressed air to remove residual dust before painting.
